game: KC @ JAX, 2025-10-06 20:15 ET, outdoor, JAX +3.5, total 45.5

script.base: Close outdoor night game, not a blowout: KC -3.5, implied KC 24.5 / JAX 21.0, total 45.5. KC leads by a score or it is tied late, so starters finish. JAX stays Etienne-leaning on the ground (49 carries, 251 yards in weeks 2-4) but as a 3.5 dog throws more than a favorite. KC is a committee (Hunt 31 carries, Pacheco 27, Mahomes 13 in weeks 2-4) with Kelce the target leader (18 targets). Moderate pace, neither shootout nor slog.
script.flip1: KC gets up by 10+ early, runs the clock with Hunt and Pacheco, and Mahomes/Kelce/Thornton yards stall; JAX abandons the run, so Etienne's rushing line dies and BTJ/Strange/Washington targets spike.
script.flip2: Etienne controls the clock against KC's 5.24 YPC run defense, holds KC's offense off the field, and it becomes a low-possession grind: KC skill overs miss and the total leans under. Weather could force this, but no forecast is saved.

pre_mortem: It's Monday and the Kelce over lost. JAX bracketed him, Mahomes threw at the 13 explosives they allow (Thornton 354 air yards, Brown 146) instead of the middle, and the 26-yard week repeated because Abdullah was never the TE matcher. The 45-yard pace was the tell. Etienne over 97.5 would have lost the same way the rate said it would: a normal 16-carry day at a 5-yard average lands in the mid-80s, and 97.5 only falls on the 124/143 spikes. The under would have lost the other way, on one of the 15 chunk runs KC has already allowed. Both counters were at least as strong as the reads, which is why Etienne is a pass and Kelce is an unsized flag.
slip_story: No slip. A 24.5-21 script does not yield two legs that clear their medians after scheme, pace and pre-mortem. Kelce over would need KC to throw; Etienne rush over would need JAX to run through a KC lead; a total under would fight the same-game receiving over. House rules: no TDs, one market per player, no depth-receiver legs. Read only. No bet placed.
